reviews.review:
As a huge fan of Back 4 Blood, I've waded through some of its negative and positive reception and found a game that, while flawed, had so much to offer if you gave it a real chance. As someone who loved the Left 4 Dead series, I saw Back 4 Blood as a solid modern alternative. It is one of the few games I followed closely before launch because I was excited about it.

The gunplay was highly satisfying due to the sound effects, animations, and overall feel, and the weapon and character customization was top-notch, allowing you to change weapon attachments, skins, clothing items, etc. The special infected, while sometimes hard to distinguish in the heat of battle, had some really cool designs, adding to the intensity of the horde fights. Their overall lore and design were unique for a zombie game.

One of the most underrated aspects of the game was the card system, which became my favorite feature as it allowed for tons of experimentation and builds to play with. The flexibility to mix and match cards to suit your playstyle was a game-changer for me, giving the gameplay an extra layer of depth. The card system was controversial but brought a tactical element that kept me returning for more, as just about any card combination worked. Yes, some were better, but it allowed players to customize their class and come up with some, at times, OP builds that were so fun to play with. The difficulty curve was brutal at first, but once things were better balanced and I "got good," it reminded me of the intensity of Helldivers, where hordes could overwhelm your team in a heartbeat if you weren't careful. That fear of getting wiped out made the gameplay thrilling, especially with friends screaming into the microphone and almost getting wiped.

The DLCs were mostly a win for me, adding tons of new content and campaigns that helped freshen up the experience. Each introduced new enemies, locations, cards, and other excellent cosmetics, but the game's PvP mode fell short. It had potential and was fun for a few hours, but it wasn't fleshed out enough to keep players engaged long-term. Like most people said, it should have included a versus campaign or a proper survival mode. Instead, we got a PVP survival mode where players control either humans or infected in a small survival arena. As I said, it was enjoyable, but the lack of a proper versus campaign really hurt the longevity.
One area where Back 4 Blood really disappointed me was the story and characters. I didn't connect with the idea of a squad of zombie killers reclaiming the earth. It felt too heroic for a zombie game, where I prefer the grittier, no-hope kind of narrative that leaves you feeling like survival is the only goal, not victory. The story lacked the bleakness I expected in a world overrun by the undead. Some of the characters were cool. I wish they had received more development and backstories, but they're more like Expendables movie characters with one-liners and sometimes annoying dialogue.

While Back 4 Blood could have been better and lived up to the hype for many, I personally appreciated the effort and had a great time with the parts that worked, which was most of the game. It's sad to see it labeled a failure, as I was genuinely excited for the future of this game. It could have evolved into something extraordinary with more support and players. For fans who stuck with it, there was a lot to love. While a part of me says don't buy it as it's not getting any more updates and it's a dead game, another part says buy it and give it a chance if you like Helldivers and Left 4 Dead. You'd really like this game with the gun customization of every shooter from the past 15 years. It's such a shame that there will not be more updates, as it is painful to see such a great gem of a game fall by the wayside. Do yourself a favor: Buy this game (preferable on sale), get some friends together, and play this game. I promise it's quite a special game.
